variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start in A: move to the top of the visible button to prepare. Select A whenever the hand is not yet in the prepared position. The prepared pose in these observations has the wrist above the button, height approximately 0.15, and closed fingers; do not mistake the wrist's image position for the fingertips' contact point. Once prepared, choose between B and C using the updated passage_count and the requested ordinal N from the goal. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. If passage_count equals N-1 and the next target passage is approximately 35 or fewer time units away, select C. Estimate the upcoming arrival using the updated motion_history, including retained and newly shown samples, and the currently visible target x. Fit smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to those timestamped cube positions and find its next target crossing after the current final observation. Account for slowing and reversal at endpoints; do not extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant. When passage_count equals N-1 and that crossing is approximately 35 or fewer time units away, select C even if the cube is still near an endpoint. A short or nearly stationary current interval does not by itself imply that the crossing is farther away. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. Apply the uncertainty fallback only after estimating timing from the full updated motion_history, not merely because the current interval is short or nearly stationary. If timing remains uncertain after considering that history, select B and refine the estimate from the next observations rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.

fields.name: passage_count
fields.description: Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side. Compute the sign of cube x minus target x. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. Ignore exact equality until a nonzero side appears. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: The number of completed target-center passages by the cube up to and including this decision's final observation. Count passages in both directions, including during preparation; do not count proximity alone. A passage occurs when cube x minus target x changes sign along the continuous motion. Initialize to 0. The values by decision step are: episode 23: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 32: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 66: 0,0,1,1; episode 94: 0,0,1,2,2; episode 99: 0,0,1,1. e.g. 2

fields.name: last_side
fields.description: The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
fields.annotation: The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1

fields.name: motion_history
fields.description: Maintain an ordered list of timestamped cube-center execution observations, each written [timestamp, [y, x]]. With empty memory, start with all execution observations currently shown. Otherwise copy the incoming list and append all newly shown execution observations through the current final observation, including observations during A and B. Exclude demonstration observations. Retain earlier samples in chronological order and do not duplicate a timestamp already stored. Write observed positions only, without predicting the selected command's effects. Retained samples provide motion timing when the current interval is short or nearly stationary. e.g. [[0, [137, 47]], [16, [131, 80]], [32, [119, 147]]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of timestamped cube-center observations from execution through this decision's final observation. Each sample is [timestamp, [y, x]]. Initialize with the execution observations shown at the first decision, then append newly shown execution observations at every decision, including observations during preparation and waiting. Exclude demonstration observations. Retain earlier samples in chronological order and include each timestamp only once. Record observed positions only, never future positions or effects expected from the command selected at this decision. e.g. [[0, [137, 47]], [16, [131, 80]], [32, [119, 147]]]

history.critique:
field motion_history, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  When stopping on the second or third target passage, a decision near an endpoint showed only two nearly stationary cube positions. The policy chose B rather than C although passage_count and last_side correctly identified the next passage as the requested one. Earlier motion timing had disappeared, breaking SUFFICIENCY: the remaining observations could not establish the time to return to the target. Add motion_history, an ordered list of timestamped cube-center observations from execution through the current decision's final observation. Initialize it with the initial execution observation and append newly observed samples at every decision, including motion during preparation and waiting. Each sample is [timestamp, [y, x]]; retain chronological order and include each timestamp only once. For example: [[0, [137, 47]], [16, [131, 80]], [32, [119, 147]]]. This field records observed motion, never future positions or the effects expected from the selected command. Leave passage_count and last_side unchanged.

field motion_history, POLICY PROMPT
  When the requested passage was next, a short interval at an endpoint contained too little motion to determine whether pressing should begin. The policy waited despite correct passage_count and last_side because earlier timing was not carried forward. This breaks SUFFICIENCY. Maintain motion_history as an ordered list of timestamped cube-center observations, each written [timestamp, [y, x]]. With empty memory, start with the execution observations currently shown. Otherwise copy the incoming list and append all newly shown execution observations in chronological order, including observations during A and B; do not duplicate a timestamp already stored. Write the resulting list through the current final observation, without predicting the selected command's effects. For example: [[0, [137, 47]], [16, [131, 80]], [32, [119, 147]]]. Retain earlier samples so short or motionless current intervals can still be interpreted using the observed oscillation. Keep the existing passage_count and last_side updates.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  For goals requiring the second or third passage, the policy selected B at a turnaround even though the updated count correctly made the upcoming crossing the requested passage. Only two almost stationary positions were newly visible. The instruction to estimate timing from the current interval, together with the uncertainty fallback to B, could not distinguish a fast turnaround requiring C from a slower one requiring B; this breaks SUFFICIENCY. Replace the current-interval-only timing instruction with an instruction to estimate oscillation from the updated motion_history, including both retained and newly shown samples, using their timestamps and the currently visible target position. Fit the smooth periodic motion over that history and find the next future target crossing, accounting for endpoint reversal rather than extrapolating near-zero velocity. Keep the existing ordinal gate and approximately 35-time-unit lead window: choose C when passage_count equals N-1 and the next crossing lies within that window, including when the cube is still near an endpoint. Choose B when the ordinal gate is not met or arrival is farther away. Apply the uncertainty fallback only after considering the retained history, not merely because the current interval is short or stationary. Remove episode-specific turnaround references; replace them with this observable timing rule. Preparation, crossing-count updates, and the lack of supplied points for menu options remain unchanged.

Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. Apply the uncertainty fallback only after estimating timing from the full updated motion_history, not merely because the current interval is short or nearly stationary. If timing remains uncertain after considering that history, select B and refine the estimate from the next observations rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.

fields.name: passage_count
fields.description: Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side. Compute the sign of cube x minus target x. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. Ignore exact equality until a nonzero side appears. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: The number of completed target-center passages by the cube up to and including this decision's final observation. Count passages in both directions, including during preparation; do not count proximity alone. A passage occurs when cube x minus target x changes sign along the continuous motion. Initialize to 0. The values by decision step are: episode 23: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 32: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 66: 0,0,1,1; episode 94: 0,0,1,2,2; episode 99: 0,0,1,1. e.g. 2

fields.name: last_side
fields.description: The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
fields.annotation: The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1

fields.name: motion_history
fields.description: Maintain an ordered list of timestamped cube-center execution observations, each written [timestamp, [y, x]]. With empty memory, start with all execution observations currently shown. Otherwise copy the incoming list and append all newly shown execution observations through the current final observation, including observations during A and B. Exclude demonstration observations. Retain earlier samples in chronological order and do not duplicate a timestamp already stored. Write observed positions only, without predicting the selected command's effects. Retained samples provide motion timing when the current interval is short or nearly stationary. e.g. [[0, [137, 47]], [16, [131, 80]], [32, [119, 147]]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of timestamped cube-center observations from execution through this decision's final observation. Each sample is [timestamp, [y, x]]. Initialize with the execution observations shown at the first decision, then append newly shown execution observations at every decision, including observations during preparation and waiting. Exclude demonstration observations. Retain earlier samples in chronological order and include each timestamp only once. Record observed positions only, never future positions or effects expected from the command selected at this decision. e.g. [[0, [137, 47]], [16, [131, 80]], [32, [119, 147]]]
